Adding a digital version of your driver's license to your iPhone looks set to roll out to a 15th US state in the near future.

Apple currently lists 14 states, plus the territory of Puerto Rico, that support the feature, with backend assets suggesting another state is on the way……

Many of us have long hoped for a future where we don't need to carry physical identification documents like a driver's license or passport, and can instead simply present digital ID on an iPhone or Apple Watch.

That future may still be some way off, but Apple took its first steps back in 2021, when it announced plans to let iPhone users add their driver's license or state ID to the Wallet app. That feature is now supported in 14 states:

  • Arizona
  • Arkansas
  • California
  • Colorado
  • Georgia
  • Hawaii
  • Illinois
  • Iowa
  • Maryland
  • Montana
  • New Mexico
  • North Dakota
  • Ohio
  • West Virginia

Backend assets discovered by MacRumors suggest Oklahoma will soon be joining that list.

We recently detailed the steps to add a driver's license or state ID to the iPhone's Wallet app. As we noted at the time, it's worth being aware that a digital ID is not a complete replacement for the physical document, so unfortunately we still recommend continuing to carry that "crumpled" version.

That said, the digital version can still help protect your privacy at eligible TSA checkpoints and when proving your age to businesses. The ID will confirm you meet the age requirement without disclosing any personal details, like your date of birth.
